newsitem.title: USA: British-U.S. team wins howitzer contract.
newsitem.headline: British-U.S. team wins howitzer contract.

text.p: A defense contracting team comprised of Britain's Vickers Plc and Textron Inc of the United States has won a $39.6 million contract to develop a new howitzer for the U.S. military, the Army said on Tuesday.

Engineering development work on the light, mobile 155mm gun will be completed in 1999. Analysts estimate that the weapon could eventually provide $500 million in sales to the U.S. Army and Marine Corps for the team.
The development work will be done in New Orleans by the Textron Marine & Land Systems Division of Cadillac Gage Textron and by Vickers Shipbuilding and Engineering Ltd. a unit of Vickers Plc.
The Marine Corps said in a release that the winning team edged out a contracting team led by United Defense Limited Partnership of Minneapolis and Royal Ordnance, a unit of British Aerospace Plc.

British officials have pressed the United States on the howitzer competitionm, noting that London has in recent years purchased far more U.S.-built weaponary for British forces than the United States has bought from British defense firms.

The new howitzer, known as the LW155, will replace the current M198 towed howitzer in both the U.S. Army and Marine Corps with one that is nearly half of the weight, yet performs equal to or better than the M198, the Marine Corps said.

During the three-year engineering development phase, the Vickers-Textron team will build eight prototypes of the gun and will make design changes during extensive testing over the period, the Marine Corps said.
